proposed_widenings.name: passive_class_feature
proposed_widenings.justification: Ritual Adept is always-on from level 1. It has no activation event, no use count, and no reset cadence. The surface only has 'activation' family for ClassFeatureMechanics, which requires activationCost + UseCountResource + RestResetCadence + ClassFeatureEffect. Forcing those onto a permanently-active rule modifier would be dishonest.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You can cast any spell as a Ritual if that spell has the Ritual tag and the spell is in your spellbook. You needn't have the spell prepared...

proposed_widenings.name: modify_casting_rule
proposed_widenings.justification: The effect is not granting new spells (grant_spell_access) but modifying how existing spellbook entries may be cast: removes the preparation requirement for Ritual-tagged spells, replacing it with a physical-book requirement. No v4 effect atom covers a casting-constraint modification.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You needn't have the spell prepared, but you must read from the book to cast a spell in this way.

notes: The primary blocker is structural: ClassFeatureMechanics has no 'passive' family. Even if it did, the effect 'modify_casting_rule' (remove preparation constraint, add spellbook-in-hand constraint, for ritual-tagged spells) does not map to any existing ClassFeatureEffect variant. The closest v4 atom is grant_spell_access but that covers granting access to spell lists, not modifying how a subset of already-owned spells may be cast.
